item.title: Yankees predicted to replace Austin Wells with Cubs free agent catcher
item.description: Yankees predicted to replace Austin Wells with Cubs free agent catcher originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees are in the market for a right-handed hitting catcher. They can keep Ali Sanchez around as depth, but they should target a better hitter to platoon with Austin Wells. Overall, Wells had a disappointing 2026 season. Offensively, he hit .186/.292/.332 with 14 home runs and a .624 OPS. As their everyday backstop, the Yankees were likely hoping for much more. To help fix their lack of production from behind the plate, Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter predicted the Yankees will sign an 11-year veteran who spent the past two seasons with the Chicago Cubs . "The Yankees got a .196 average and .600 OPS from the catcher position last season, including a 74 OPS+ from incumbent starter Austin Wells. "With a .122/.192/.244 line against left-handed pitching, they at least need to find him a right-handed hitting platoon partner, and veteran Carson Kelly would be a clear upgrade," Reuter wrote. Kelly can help solve New York's problems against left-handed pitching. He hit .298 with a .375 OBP and .871 OPS in 121 at-bats versus southpaws last year. MORE : Padres interested in re-signing 2.86 ERA starter despite $32M contract decision He loses some value against right-handers, hitting .239 with a .639 OPS in 259 at-bats. The Yankees won't have to break the bank to sign Kelly, but he may be looking for a full-time catching gig instead of a part-time role in free agency. Either way, a one-to two-year deal seems to be in the cards for the 32-year-old, and the Yankees are a logical landing spot. item.title: Report card: Bills beat Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving
item.description: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs on their way to a 13-10 victory on Thanksgiving night. The Bills muddled through a chilly, rain-soaked game to win with a last-second field goal from Tyler Bass. Buffalo's aerial attack was grounded by the weather. Quarterback Josh Allen struggled through most of the game, throwing two interceptions and several inaccurate passes. While the abysmal conditions limited the passing attack, it did send the Bills back to an old-school ground-and-pound attack. James Cook rushed 32 times and scored the Bills only touchdown. The defense kept the Chiefs from gaining any sort of rhythm. Buffalo allowed only one touchdown, which was an Emmett Johnson one-yard dive on the opening drive of the second half. The Bills benefited from a Harrison Butker miss, which gave the Bills some life as the fourth quarter continued. Bass was good from 54 and 57 yards in the fourth quarter, ultimately giving Buffalo its seventh consecutive victory. Here is how Bills Wire grades the Thanksgiving performance: Passing offense: F The weather conditions were horrendous for any sort of explosive plays to be completed through the air. Even still, there was hope that Allen would be a little better than a 10-of-21 passing day. Allen totaled only 81 yards through the air. Both of Allen's interceptions were inaccurate balls that led to the turnovers. It was disappointing that Joe Brady could not figure out something to get a bit more out of the passing attack. Thank goodness for the defense and James Cook; otherwise, this game would have been a Kansas City victory. Khalil Shakir led the Bills with three catches for 33 yards. Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore, and Ty Johnson each reeled in two passes. Patrick Mahomes, playing in the same exact conditions (obviously), doubled-up Allen, throwing for 174 yards. It was possible to move the ball a bit through the air. Allen just didn't do it. Rushing offense: A- James Cook is usurping Allen's spot as Buffalo's offensive MVP. Cook was patient, setting up runs and battling for any additional yards he could obtain. He rushed 32 times, which was half of the number of the Bills offensive plays on the game. Cook totaled 117 yards, good for a 3.7-yard-per-carry average. He scurried into the end zone for Buffalo's lone touchdown on the day. Allen rushed seven times for 43 yards. As has been customary for Buffalo, the Bills succeeded on several short-yardage attempts with Allen quarterback dives. The Bills lack a rushing option beyond Cook in the backfield. Ray Davis managed six yards on four carries. Pass defense: A- Buffalo's pass defense did a solid job of limiting the Chiefs. Kansas City did make a few decent plays with Travis Kelce finding space against Buffalo's secondary. However, for the most part, the Bills won more of the battles. The allowed the Chiefs to convert only two-of-eleven third-down attempts. Davison Igbinosun and Max Hairston held strong as the starting cornerbacks. With Christian Benford

item.title: Shocking thrashing! Schalke 04 crushed by Paderborn in promoted sides' clash
item.description: SC Paderborn 07 v FC Schalke 04 - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Striker Edin Dzeko returned to the starting line-up, but Bundesliga newcomers Schalke 04 suffered a humiliating defeat a week before the Ruhr derby against Borussia Dortmund. Miron Muslic's alarmingly poor side lost 8-1 (3-0) away to fellow promoted side SC Paderborn, extending their winless run to eight competitive matches. Paderborn claimed their third home victory and moved into mid-table for the time being. Jano ter Horst put the hosts ahead with his first goal of the season (21). Stefano Marino scored a hat-trick (39, 45+4, 57), while Steffen Tigges (55), Deniz Zeitler (73), Gabriel Vidovic (85, penalty) and Felix Götze (90+6) also found the net. Adil Aouchiche scored Schalke's consolation goal (59). Last season, the Gelsenkirchen club had narrowly won both meetings in the second division. Muslic said Schalke wanted to approach the match "with great responsibility and unity", but they squandered a huge early chance. Junior Adamu got a shot away after a mistake by Mattes Hansen, only for goalkeeper Nahuel Noll to save (2). The 15,000 spectators in the sold-out arena saw the hosts make the more active, if nervier, start. Marino had the best chance after a counter-attack, but Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius saved (17). Schalke then had to replace Junior Dina Ebimbe, who injured his thigh during a footrace without any contact from an opponent (20). Shortly afterwards, ter Horst scored following a free-kick. Schalke offered little. Dzeko, a peripheral figure in the Bundesliga up to that point, barely made an impression either. "I can't make allowances based on names," Muslic had said before the match, but he nevertheless started the 40-year-old for the third time this season. The visitors perked up after conceding, with Hasan Kurucay's shot going narrowly wide (33). Paderborn, though, kept finding gaps in the second-division champions' usually solid defence. Marino fired well over in the 34th minute, but the East Westphalian side's top scorer doubled the lead shortly afterwards with a superb solo run, then struck again in stoppage time. Schalke came out with a little more energy after the break, but Paderborn repeatedly caught them on the counter-attack.

item.title: Undermanned Bayern held at Hamburg after Kimmich sees red
item.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich walks off after his red card against Hamburg on Saturday. (Ibrahim OT) Injury-ravaged Bayern Munich were held to a scoreless draw away at Hamburg in the Bundesliga on Saturday, with captain Joshua Kimmich sent off in the first half for a hair pull, while Schalke fell to a calamitous 8-1 loss at Paderborn. The draw, Bayern's second in two league games, leaves them a point behind league leaders Borussia Dortmund, who host Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday. Kimmich's moment of madness is the latest setback in a horror week in the Bavarian capital. In addition to their injury woes, club executives have been sharply criticised after launching a public campaign to pressure midfielder Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Bayern lost their first match of the season with a 2-1 defeat away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. Coming into the match, Bayern had won 14 of their past 16 matches with Hamburg and had not tasted defeat against them since 2009. Bayern had travelled to Hamburg with a decimated forward line, missing five attacking players including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane through injury. Bayern's lack of forward options was obvious from the opening minute, with the defending champions dominating possession but reduced to taking long-range efforts on goal. The visitors' hopes of an unlikely win took a hit just before the break, when Kimmich was shown a straight red for pulling Alexander Rossing-Lelesiit's hair. Clear goal chances were few and far between for both sides in the second half, with Bayern's appeals for a stoppage-time penalty for a foul on Luis Diaz waved away. The Bavarian giants will look to get back to winning ways when they host high-flying Hertha Berlin, who are on track for promotion after winning 12 of their 13 Bundesliga 2 games this season, in the German Cup on Tuesday. Elsewhere on Saturday, Paderborn thumped struggling Schalke 8-1 to more than double the biggest Bundesliga win in their history. Stefano Marino scored three while Jano ter Horst, Steffen Tigges, Deniz Zeitler, Gabriel Vidovic and Felix Goetze also got on the scoresheet in the romp. Schalke, who were promoted in the summer, host arch-rivals Dortmund next week. Mainz scored twice in the final five minutes to sink Union Berlin 2-1 at home, leaving the capital club in the automatic relegation places. Cologne cruised to a 5-0 home victory over promoted Elversberg, with Marius Buelter hitting a hat-trick and Germany winger Said El Mala bagging a brace. Later on Saturday, Stuttgart hope to rebound from their midweek Champions League loss at Inter Milan when they host Eintracht Frankfurt. dwi/nf

item.title: A silly red card and more injuries - Hamburg and Bayern settle for a goalless draw
item.description: A silly red card and more injuries - Hamburg and Bayern settle for a goalless draw The revived Nord-Süd-Klassiker ended without goals on Saturday, yet there was no shortage of drama at a sold-out Volksparkstadion. While Mario Vušković celebrated a clean sheet on his emotional Bundesliga debut for Hamburger SV, a youthful FC Bayern side saw Joshua Kimmich dismissed before halftime and Konrad Laimer limp off late on in a hard-fought 0-0 stalemate. Here is our full match report: Match report: HSV vs. FC Bayern The afternoon began on an emotional note for the hosts, as Mario Vušković was handed his first-ever Bundesliga start after club captain Nicolás Capaldo failed to recover in time. Alongside him, 17-year-old left-back Louis Lemke - born after HSV’s last top-flight victory over Bayern - helped anchor a backline immediately tested by the visitors. Vincent Kompany named Bayern’s youngest Bundesliga starting XI in over eight-and-a-half years, and the absence of sidelined stars Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Jamal Musiala, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Luis Díaz, who was on the bench at least, was evident in the final third. While Bayern controlled the tempo and possession and carved out more opportunities, they lacked their usual cutting edge to punish the “Rothosen”. Just as it seemed the sides would head into the dressing rooms on even terms, the match boiled over in the 44th minute. Following a shove and provocation from HSV talent Alexander Røssing-Lelesiit, Joshua Kimmich reacted by lightly pulling the HSV attacker's hair, leaving the referee with little choice but to brandish a straight red card. In immediate response to going down to ten men, Kompany turned to his bench for the start of the second half, introducing Colombian winger Luis Díaz to inject much-needed firepower. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Bayern started the second period brightly. However, the story of the first half persisted: the champions progressed into the final third with relative ease, yet consistently lacked the sharp movement, positioning, and clinical finishing required to beat Daniel Heuer Fernandes. As the clock ticked down, Hamburg grew increasingly dangerous on the break, with Fábio Vieira, Albert Grønbæk, and Martin Adeline all coming close to snatching a famous winner. Compounding Bayern’s difficult afternoon, second-half substitute Konrad Laimer was forced off with an injury in the 87th minute , raising further questions about an injury curse hovering over Kompany’s squad. Bayern briefly appealed for a late penalty just before the final whistle when Díaz went down inside the box, but the referee waved play on. For Vušković, meanwhile, walking off with a clean sheet against the German record champions marked a dream start to his Bundesliga career as the contest finished 0-0.

item.title: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr.
item.description: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr. originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays missed out on Tarik Skubal, and they missed out on Teruaki Sato this offseason. But they've already begun to pivot, landing Kaima Taira and Jazz Chisholm Jr. While those are two notable additions, the Blue Jays might not be close to being done. They offered Skubal $400 million, and the Taira and Chisholm deals aren't even close to half their offer to Skubal. So, it shouldn't be a surprise if they get involved elsewhere. Andy McCullough of The Athletic named the Blue Jays as the "ideal landing spot" for free-agent Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki. Even after landing Chisholm, the Blue Jays would be a great landing spot for Suzuki this offseason. Seiya Suzuki's 'ideal' landing spot is with Blue Jays "The Blue Jays have money to spend and a zeal to spend it," McCullough writes. "... The team needs more outfield help, and Suzuki has been a steady performer since arriving in America in 2022." Chisholm will help out the Blue Jays' infield, but this team could use help in the outfield. Jonatan Clase, Brett Bateman and Nathan Lukes could all start for the Blue Jays in the outfield next season. While there is some appeal to all three, adding an elite hitter like Suzuki, who has the ability to hit 26 home runs and also control the strike zone, would be an incredible pickup for the Blue Jays this offseason. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news Suzuki might be a little bit older, at 32 years old; he's coming off a strong 2026 season in which he had a .270 batting average with 26 homers, 5.1 bWAR, and elite defense in the outfield. With the Cubs landing Sato this offseason, it would seem Suzuki might not return to the Cubs this offseason, especially with Suzuki likely to seek a $120 million deal like what Sato got. It might be a lot of money for the Blue Jays to spend on Suzuki, but with their willingness to spend big this offseason, overpaying a little bit to guarantee they land Suzuki, arguably the best bat available this offseason, would make a lot of sense. Being able to add both Suzuki and Chisholm in one offseason would be quite the haul for the Blue Jays. Chisholm's deal wasn't too expensive, so a big Suzuki contract wouldn't hurt as bad if they land the Cubs star outfielder. item.title: Farrell says low crowd in Ireland win 'a shame'
item.description: Farrell is not convinced on the merits of kicking off finals weekend with a Friday double-header [Getty Images] Ireland head coach Andy Farrell said it was a "shame" his side's Nations Championship victory over Australia was played in front of a low crowd at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium. Friday night's fifth-place play-off attracted an attendance of just 32,000 with the uppermost tier of the 82,000-capacity stadium entirely closed. Ireland beat the Wallabies 38-14 after Italy overcame Fiji on the first day of the inaugural competition's finals day weekend at the home of England rugby. Ticket sales for Saturday and Sunday's action, which are headlined by England v New Zealand and the final between South Africa and France, have been stronger, but Farrell questioned the Friday night double-bill. "I'd love to spend some time to have a think about it, I've been preparing a team and you're busy doing that," he said. "But off the top of my head, I don't know whether the Friday night thing works or being at the same venue. If we'd have played at the Aviva (Stadium in Dublin), it would have been full. "They look like little things, but they're not, they mean a lot to the fans, like when you don't know where your team's playing and then you're trying to get a flight and all of a sudden they're £1,700. It doesn't fit." Farrell senses 'shift' as Ireland finish 2026 strongly Ulster resurgence aids Ireland's perfect November Format 'doesn't make sense' Farrell said he enjoyed parts of the spectacle, which included a pre-game performance from British popstar Myles Smith. "I love what they're trying to do. I love the razzmatazz and coming into the ground it felt different. It felt like it was trying to be like an event, like a concert," he added. "It was just a shame that we couldn't get the people through the door. The pre-match hype looked fantastic on the TV – from what I saw in the dressing room anyway. "The 16:40 game – I felt for those boys really. And Sam Prendergast didn't get anything for man of the match, so playing for fifth place obviously didn't mean much." Ireland won five of their six pool games to finish third in the northern hemisphere table behind France and England, while Australia finished third in the southern hemisphere standings behind South Africa and New Zealand after losing four matches. "It's strange, it doesn't make sense," Farrell said. "But it's not our jobs to make sense of it. It's our job to just keep playing what's in front of our faces." item.title: Why Marc Marquez was penalised for leaving the Valencia grid - although he did nothing wrong
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez’s final MotoGP sprint race on Saturday was disrupted by a problem beyond his control and by a penalty that affected his result. It was a penalty many fans disagreed with, judging by its jeering reception from the crowd at Valencia. The start of the final sprint race of the 2026 season was delayed by a problem rarely seen before: an issue with the lights. The red lights took too long to go out, prompting complaints from the entire grid, who raised their hands to signal that the start procedure was taking far too long. Read Also: Marc Marquez's Ducati catches fire in aborted Valencia GP sprint start In truth, there had already been delays in race control procedures over the weekend. As early as Q2, it was noticeable that it took far too long for a yellow flag to be displayed following a crash by Ai Ogura in the final minutes. In fact, Marco Bezzecchi had time to pass that point, eight seconds after the crash, without encountering the signal, which was displayed a further two seconds later. This is what allowed him to secure pole position without losing his best lap time, as would have been stipulated by the FIM sporting regulations were a yellow flag displayed. Read Also: MotoGP Valencia GP: Marco Bezzecchi scorches to pole position, Marc Marquez second However, the delay in the start caused even more of a mess. Today’s MotoGP bikes are prototypes not designed to be stationary, when the lack of cooling quickly causes their systems to overheat. That is exactly what happened to Marquez’s Ducati, which was in second position on the starting grid. Whilst the other bikes remained unaffected, the Italian machine began to emit a noticeable amount of smoke. Marc tried to start his bike, mainly to get some fresh air to it, but was unable to do so. The Ducati then caught fire, causing Marquez to throw himself off it in a bid to avoid being burnt. However, he still indicated that he had sustained some injuries, with parts of his leathers charred black. As a result, the bike was rendered unusable and had to be put out by the fire brigade using an extinguisher. Marquez headed straight for the pits, as did the bike he was due to start the race on, and went to collect the second one, already prepared by his team - whilst the sprint start was cancelled under a red flag due to the incident. item.description: Sebastian Vettel's damning recollection of his Ferrari days. (Source: MEGA) Four-time F1 world champion Sebastian Vettel has shared a damning verdict on his time at Ferrari. The German former racing driver stated that the team lacked the courage to make major changes and hence found itself being beaten by the likes of Mercedes regularly during his time at the team. “I think what I learned during my time is that perhaps Ferrari lacked a bit of courage to change in that respect,” Vettel told Nextgen-Auto . “We're too tense, we're not relaxed, we're not having as much fun. But much like many drivers before and after him, he national found it incredibly difficult to change the culture at Maranello and bring the team back to winning ways. In his six seasons at Ferrari, Vettel won 14 races but failed to win a drivers’ title or take Ferrari back to the top of the constructors’ standings. His best results came in 2017 and 2018, as he finished runner-up to Lewis Hamilton on both occasions, with an early-season title challenge coming crashing down in the latter half of both years. item.title: F1's latest feud heats up following another tense on-track encounter
item.description: Carlos Sainz has once again taken issue with Franco Colapinto 's on-track behaviour following an incident during FP2 at the Qatar Grand Prix, just a week after a similar encounter in Las Vegas. While the feuds between Max Verstappen and George Russell and between the two Ferrari drivers have been among the most heated in recent weeks, tensions have also been growing between Sainz and Colapinto. The pair had already been involved in a tense moment down the Strip in Las Vegas, when the Argentine attempted an aggressive move during free practice, coming dangerously close to making contact with the Williams driver. During FP2 yesterday, Colapinto picked up Sainz's slipstream down the main straight before attacking the Spaniard down the inside at Turn 1. The Argentine ran wide under braking, forcing his rival to move aside to avoid contact. The incident also caught the attention of an amused George Russell, who laughed over the team radio. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Speaking to the media on Friday in Qatar, Sainz questioned the Alpine driver's approach to practice sessions, suggesting that such aggression was unnecessary given that there was nothing at stake: “It’s been a couple of Fridays that Franco has been a bit difficult with me, and I don’t understand what he’s doing on Fridays.” He then added: “He races like it’s Sunday, but I guess he’s just young.” When asked whether he would speak to Colapinto about his behaviour, the Spaniard replied: “Maybe I’ll say something.” Colapinto has been involved in more contentious incidents with other drivers this season. One such example came in Baku, where the Argentine triggered a three-car collision at Turn 1 following a Safety Car restart, taking himself, Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris out of the race. Norris, usually rather composed when speaking to the media, lost his patience on that occasion, going as far as to say: “Just some drivers that shouldn’t be in F1 , to be honest.” A few days later, having had time to cool down, Norris publicly apologised to the Alpine driver in a social media post, revealing that the pair had already spoken privately and cleared the air. Even Colapinto's own boss, Flavio Briatore, made no attempt to defend the Argentine on that occasion, describing the incident as a “very poor move for a driver of his experience” and publicly apologising to Norris and McLaren.

item.title: Rampant Köln dismantle Elversberg 5-0 to spark European dreams
item.description: Rampant Köln dismantle Elversberg 5-0 to spark European dreams Carrying the momentum from their hard-earned draw in Munich straight onto their home turf, 1. FC Köln delivered an attacking masterclass to sweep aside SV Elversberg 5-0 on Saturday. With Marius Bülter bagging a memorable hat-trick and Said El Mala adding two goals of his own, the Billy Goats produced a statement performance that will have supporters at the RheinEnergieSTADION starting to dream of the European places. Here is our full match report: Match report: 1. FC Köln vs. SV Elversberg Köln grabbed the very first goal of the Bundesliga afternoon inside eight minutes through textbook tactical execution. Winning the ball back high up the pitch with aggressive counter-pressing, the hosts worked the ball to Borna Sosa in the half-space, and the full-back whipped in an inviting cross for Marius Bülter to nod home from close range . The hosts kept their foot on the gas and doubled their advantage in the 16th minute through a slick piece of link-up play. Mikey Moore and Said El Mala combined neatly to carve open the Elversberg penalty area, with Moore laying the ball off for El Mala to rifle an unstoppable finish from roughly seven meters past the defender and goalkeeper Nicolas Kristof into the top corner. René Wagner’s men effectively put the contest to bed in the 39th minute with a carbon copy of their opener. Once again, Sosa delivered a pinpoint cross from the half-space, and once again, Bülter beat his marker to head home for 3-0 - giving Köln their largest halftime cushion since 2023. Back then, Köln beat Werder Bremen 7-1 - how high could the scoreline get this time around? Rather than sitting back on their three-goal cushion after the restart, Köln continued to press forward and put the result beyond all doubt in the 63rd minute. El Mala nearly capped off a blistering counter-attack himself, only for Kristof to rush far off his line to deny the Köln talisman; however, the loose ball fell straight into the path of Bülter, who kept his composure to fire home from distance and complete his hat-trick. Just five minutes later, El Mala got his second goal of the afternoon to make it 5-0. Center-back Joël Schmied surged forward down the right flank and squared the ball across to El Mala, who found himself completely unmarked in the center of the box and slotted home calmly. With five goals on the board, Köln finally took their foot off the gas in the closing stages, yet Elversberg remained unable to salvage even a consolation. The visitors’ best opening fell to young talent Francis Onyeka, who hesitated too long when deciding where to place his effort, allowing Marvin Schwäbe to close the angle and make a comfortable save. Köln now move level with Elversberg on 13 points - leaving the Müngersdorf faithful with plenty of reason to glance upward toward the European spots.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
